messages:
Ava: Quick copy review — this empty state shows when a team's token quota is exhausted. current mock: — Header: "Quota exceeded" — Body: "You've used all available tokens for this billing period. Generations are paused until your quota resets or you request more." — Primary CTA: "Upgrade plan" — Secondary: "Learn about quotas" I think the tone feels a bit scary and the CTA is ambiguous for enterprise users. Thoughts? :thinking_face: Mateo: Agree. Two concerns: (1) "Upgrade plan" implies only paid paths — we have customers on committed Dedicated pools who need to request overrides, (2) accessibility: screen readers need a clearer action label. Jin: For frontend, also want short button labels for small screens. But we have an icon-only state in the compact dashboard, so full words needed for desktop. Ava: Proposed alternate microcopy (iteration A): — Header: "Token usage limit reached" — Body: "You've hit your token limit for this billing period. Generations are paused. You can request a quota increase or wait for the period to reset." — Primary CTA: "Request quota increase" — Secondary: "View quota docs" Ava: Rationale: "Request quota increase" maps to both self-serve and sales flows, less transactional than "Upgrade". Body removes "scary" words like "exceeded" and points to two clear next steps. Sam: Accessibility nit: primary CTA should have aria-label="Request quota increase — opens request form" so screen reader users know what happens. Also announce the header as role="status" so AT reads immediately. Jin: Implementation note: for small buttons we can use aria-label on the icon-only variant: aria-label="Request quota increase" and keep visible label on desktop. Also recommend focus goes to primary CTA when the empty state modal appears — reduces cognitive load. Lauren: Product question — do we want the secondary to say "View quota docs" or "How quotas work"? The latter is more friendly but longer. Mateo: I prefer "How quotas work". Short enough and more explanatory. Ava: Updated options — iteration B (final candidate): — Header: "Token limit reached" — Body: "You've reached your token limit for this billing period. Generations are paused. • Request a quota increase to continue now • Or wait until your quota resets on the first of the next period" — Primary CTA: "Request quota increase" — Secondary: "How quotas work" Ava: Also adding a small inline help text under the primary CTA: "Requests typically processed within 24–48 hours." Thoughts? Sam: +1 for the inline timing note. For screen readers, the list in the body should be a proper ul with two li elements and each li announced. Also ensure contrast of the inline note meets AA (14px regular). Jin: Technical: will ship as a small component change. Sample markup suggestion: ```html

Token limit reached

You've reached your token limit for this billing period. Generations are paused.

  • Request a quota increase to continue now
  • Wait for quota to reset on the first of the next period
How quotas work
Requests typically processed within 24–48 hours.
``` Ava: UX nit — can we avoid comma-separated numbers for timing? Use en dash "24–48 hours" (as Jin used). Small but consistent. Lauren: Approved from product side. Can we add a metric tracking event: quota_emptystate_primary_click with plan_type property? Mateo: Yes, send event. Jin can add the telemetry. Jin: Will do. Quick confirm on copy final: use iteration B content exactly, add aria-label copy as Sam suggested, and include the inline timing note. I'll open a PR targeting the empty-state component and tag @Ava for final copy sign-off. Ava: Sounds good — thanks all. :thumbsup: Mateo: Thanks! I'll update the product spec with the new label and tracking. Jin: PR opened: — review welcome. Sam: Quick accessibility follow-up: I'll run the screen reader check once PR is up. Lauren: Merging once a11y checks pass.
